clue.text: First-class accommodation for traveller in coach on way back

indicators.note: travelling on the way back means the built word is read from right to left
the coach provides accommodation for the traveller, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a coach is a bus
a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: Premium seating offered to a passenger on a coach making its return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The traveller is a sales rep, accommodated in the bus; 'on way back' turns the resulting BREPUS round. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is a synonym of excellent or top-quality.

clue.text: Supplier of rings at the jeweller's?

definitions.text: Supplier of rings at the jeweller's?

parts.words: Supplier of rings at the jeweller's?
parts.note: rings suggest wedding rings sold there, but the thing meant rings out whenever a customer opens the door

explanation.surface: A jeweller's source of wedding and engagement rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell over a shop door rings to announce each customer, so it supplies rings in the sense of chimes.

clue.text: Doctored spaniels without causing suffering

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with or altered, so the letters of the dog word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spaniels being neutered by the vet without any pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctored' looks like a vet's job on the spaniels, but it signals an anagram of SPANIELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painless is free of hurt or discomfort for the patient.

clue.text: Section of film — look-being rewound

indicators.note: a spool of film being rewound runs backwards, so the word for look is turned round

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone lecherously

explanation.surface: A clip of footage showing a lecherous glance, wound back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool or length of cinema footage.

clue.text: Trace German musician

parts.note: a grain is a tiny amount, a trace

explanation.surface: Tracking down a German composer or performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Percy Grainger was an Australian-born composer and pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Grainger was a composer and concert pianist, best known for Country Gardens.

clue.text: Moving animals around in carriages, for instance

parts.note: rolling means moving along by turning, as wheels do
stock, as in livestock, means farm animals

explanation.surface: Transporting livestock about in railway wagons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around in' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages and wagons are examples of the vehicles collectively called by this term.

clue.text: Uncovered Van Gogh's journal? It has explosive content

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Vincent was Van Gogh's first name
a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: The painter's private diary turns out to be a dangerous document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' removes the first and last letters of VINCENT, leaving INCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An incendiary is a bomb or device designed to start fires.

clue.text: Good landlords provide spirits

parts.note: a pub landlord is the host

explanation.surface: Decent publicans serve liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like drink served by landlords, but it means phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are phantoms or apparitions of the dead.

clue.text: About to get wrong answer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of giving an incorrect reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or witty reply.

clue.text: Hardy musical

definitions.meaning: ... Hardy was the stout half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Dickens's story of a workhouse orphan

explanation.surface: A sturdy, robust stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of comedian Hardy, and the title of Lionel Bart's Dickens musical.

clue.text: Period in which there's need for complete darkness

definitions.text: Period in which there's need for complete darkness

parts.words: Period in which there's need for complete darkness
parts.note: read as a description of wartime nights when all lights had to be hidden from enemy bombers

explanation.surface: A time when total darkness is required.
explanation.definitionFit: In wartime, a period when lights were extinguished or screened so no glow showed from the air.

clue.text: Lor! Teenagers rampaging in shop

indicators.note: rampaging means rushing about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as youths run riot in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lor' is an old exclamation, a form of Lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A village store selling a wide variety of goods is a shop.

clue.text: Bryson's account?

definitions.meaning: the first name of the travel writer Bryson
a statement of charges, as at a restaurant

explanation.surface: A travel writer's version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Writer Bryson's first name; also an invoice listing what is owed.

clue.text: I'll name barking dog's trainer shortly

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the word dog with the s of the possessive kept as a letter

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone promises to identify a noisy dog's handler briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' seems to be the dog's noise, but it means mad: shuffle DOGS with TRAINE ('shortly' drops the last R of trainer).
explanation.definitionFit: A designator is one who designates, so the person who will specify or name something.

clue.text: Order change of decoration

indicators.note: a change of the word means its letters are put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap the ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate is to organise or arrange things in proper relation to each other.

clue.text: In mutinous regions, Poles cease to be in control

indicators.note: mutinous means rebellious and disorderly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Polish authorities lose their hold over rebellious provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'mutinous' signals an anagram of REGIONS and POLES together.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for no longer having command or mastery of a situation.

clue.text: Organised jolly few weeks entertaining King Edward

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: June is a month, a period of a few weeks
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
Ted is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: A few weeks of fun hosting King Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts K inside JUNE to give JUNKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To junket is to go on a pleasure trip or feast, so the verb means held a jaunt.

clue.text: Load of cool people, in a way

indicators.note: the cool people are placed in the word for way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
hip means fashionable, cool
men are people

explanation.surface: Lots of trendy folk, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link before 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipment is a consignment of goods sent together, a load.

clue.text: Separate most of the long grass, making sudden discovery

parts.note: to break is to separate into pieces

indicators.note: most of the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside a golf fairway

explanation.surface: Parting the tall grass, someone stumbles on a find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH. The rough is the long grass flanking a golf course fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakthrough is an important advance or discovery made suddenly.

clue.text: Endless depression in Britain and almost all of the world

indicators.note: the shortened depression goes in the abbreviation for Britain

parts.note: GB stands for Great Britain

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a low is an area of low pressure, a weather depression

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so one letter is removed

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood grips Britain and nearly everywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts LOW to LO, which goes 'in' GB; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means relating to the whole planet, worldwide.

clue.text: Mother's captured wild animal showing a lot of bottle

indicators.note: captured means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: mam is a northern and Welsh word for mother
a gnu is a wildebeest, an African antelope

explanation.surface: Mum has caught a beast, which shows real courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, but here it is literal: a big bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount.

clue.text: Page with small picture containing c-creepy-crawly

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book

indicators.note: containing means holding the letter inside

parts.note: an inset is a small picture set within a larger one
the stammered c is a letter by itself

explanation.surface: A page with a little picture of a s-scary bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'c-' gives the letter C, which goes inside INSET.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect resembles a leaf, a kind of bug or creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Leave out refuse container

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over something
a large open bin for builders' rubbish

explanation.surface: Omit the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a skip is a large open metal bin for builders' waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit or pass over something; also a big open rubbish bin.

clue.text: Distinctive atmosphere as Dubya's wife appears topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Laura Bush is the wife of George W Bush, nicknamed Dubya

explanation.surface: A special feeling as a former First Lady appears without her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' and 'appears' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive quality or air surrounding someone.

clue.text: Accommodation a foreign girl secured in part of London

indicators.note: secured in means held inside

parts.note: Bow is a district in east London
un is a in French
gal is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from abroad has found lodgings in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an area of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a form of housing.

clue.text: Initially City's ahead, finally getting draw in important match

indicators.note: finally getting means this part comes last
initially picks out the opening letter

parts.note: up means ahead, in front, as a team leading
a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: City are leading but eventually draw a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a knockout-cup match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout cup game in football, often a high-stakes fixture.

clue.text: Rock hit originally in Welsh town

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so this piece comes first

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash
Peter means rock, from the Greek petros

explanation.surface: A rock song was first a hit in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' says LAM goes first. Lampeter is a university town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampeter is a small university town in Ceredigion, Wales.

clue.text: Behind counter spot former pin-up

indicators.note: behind means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Behind the bar stands a stain from a past glamour girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigitte Bardot was a French film star and 1960s sex symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Bardot was a French actress and famous sex symbol of the 1950s and 60s.
